title: the noise of the provider does not end a run that works, and the record of a run that did not finish is true
intent: The first live run of Yeah against a real provider on the task of the owner (the wave 41 of docs/PLAN.md 18.1) ended in the state `failed' after eight nudges, and the journal said: `the model answered with an empty message 8 times and the run ended without an effect'.  Both halves of that record were wrong.  The run had seventeen calls of tools behind it: the model read the files, searched them, ran the commands and kept the state of the work in its own head, and the provider answered every batch of those results with an empty message.  The empty message is the noise of the provider, not the refusal of the model to act: the model had acted, and the results were in front of it.  The run spent its whole budget of nudges on that noise and ended as if the model had never done anything; and the record of the run then said that it had never done anything, which is a false record that a reader of the journal cannot correct.  The wave repairs both.  The budget of the nudges pays for the nudges that no effect answered: a nudge that follows the silence of the provider after the tools of the model have come back does not spend it, because the model has acted (`yeah-turn--acted-since-nudge-p').  A model that never acts still ends: the silence that follows a silence spends the budget as before, and the run that spends it says that it did not finish.  The record of a run that did not finish names what the run did: how many times the model answered with an empty message, how many times it described its next step, and how many tools it called; a run that called its tools is no longer described as a run that ended without an effect (`yeah-turn--unfinished-payload').  The wave was found by a live run and not by an offline check, and the check that covers it plays the shape of that run with a fake transport: no network is touched, but the shape is the one that broke the harness.
objection: The wave makes the budget of the nudges mean something narrower than it meant: it pays for the nudges that no effect answered, and the silence of a provider that works is not paid for.  A model that calls its tools and then says nothing for an hour therefore never exhausts the budget, and a run under such a model can live much longer than the budget says it may.  The wave keeps the deadline of the run and the deadline of the request, so the run still ends; but the budget of the nudges is no longer a bound on the length of a run, and a caller who wants that bound must set a deadline.  The wave also trusts the count of the calls of the tools: a run whose model called a tool and then did nothing at all is a run that acts, and its silence is treated as the noise of the provider, so the record of such a run says that it called its tools and never finished, and not that it ended without an effect.  A reader of the journal must read both halves: the tools are named, and the run did not finish.  The wave does not repair the defect of the working directory of a session (`cwd' is still not applied to the tools, docs/PLAN.md 17.1), and it does not repair the shape of the provider that answers a plan instead of an action (docs/LIVE-EVIDENCE.md).  The wave does not touch the plan of the owner: the waves 41 to 44 keep their numbers and their order, and the run that found this defect was the run of the wave 41.
refuted_by: a run whose model called its tools is ended by the silence of the provider, or the silence spends the budget of the nudges; the record of a run that did not finish says that it ended without an effect although it called its tools, or it does not name the tools the run called
note: Both controls of the wave were run against the code of this wave and bit; each of them made the check fail by an assertion of the check and not by a crash of Emacs.  The control of `the-noise-of-the-provider-does-not-end-a-working-run' makes the harness forget that the model acted, and the check fails on three assertions: the run ended in the state `failed' instead of `completed', the journal holds an `unfinished' record, and the run was nudged twice instead of more than twice -- the live defect of the run of 2026-11-17, reproduced offline and end to end.  The control of `the-record-of-a-run-that-did-not-finish-is-true' makes every unfinished record claim that the run ended without an effect, and the check fails on two assertions: the record does not name the tool the run called, and the record says that the run ended without an effect although it did not.  The check itself was wrong twice before it was right: the first version collected the failures into a list with nil in it, and a list of nils is not empty, so the check could not fail; the second version read the state of the run backwards and demanded `unfinished' from a run that had finished.  The wave also found a defect of its own reasoning before the check caught it: the first version of the repair treated every silence as the noise of the provider and made the budget of the nudges meaningless for a model that never acts.  A model that never acts still ends now, and the check of that case is part of the same file.  The wave broke the control of an old claim, and the map of the method caught it: the claim `nudge-only-for-plans' removed the condition `(and (< (yeah-turn-nudges turn) (yeah-turn-max-nudges turn))' from `lib/yeah-turn.el', and the wave replaced that condition with the count of the nudges that were spent (`yeah-turn-nudge-spent'), so the control of the claim changed nothing, the verifier of the claim passed with the subject unchanged, and the claim went `inconclusive'.  The control was written against the code of the wave -- it makes the condition of the spending branch unreachable -- and it bites again: four tests of `tests/unit/test-yeah-control.el' fail on their own assertions, the run that was nudged twice is nudged zero times.  An old control is a promise that the code it names is still there, and a wave that renames a condition breaks that promise without knowing it.  The live run that found the defect is in docs/LIVE-EVIDENCE.md.
